searchText: hello what is the estimated resulting TPS for both L1 and L2 post-4844? i've seen conflicting answers but consensus seems to be neglible tps improvements to L1 and a ~100TPS improvement to L2 (from currently 600 to about 700/800) if thats true, how does the 100 TPS improvement come about i.e. how do you calculate it? <dankrad> There is no canonical way to compute TPS because Rollups can use different forms of compression. 4844 as currently suggested provides 32 kB of data per second. An uncompressed EVM rollup can turn that into about 160 tps. with compression it could be about 10x more or 1600 tps. So something like 160-1600 tps total for rollups from 4844. <dankrad> 4844 is mainly an economic improvement because rollups don't have to compete with L1 transactions anymore <icemelon> > <icemelon> I wonder if rollups will compete with each other for 4844 blobs given that each block can only hold maximal 6 blobs? (re @dankrad: 4844 is mainly an economic improvement because rollups don't have to compete with L1 transactions anymore) <dankrad> actually 3 on average. Yes rollups will compete for 4844 blobs, just as they compete for calldata now what' s that rollup that can get a 10x compression rate? <dankrad> https://twitter.com/VitalikButerin/status/1554983955182809088?lang=ms I wonder if that's purely theoretical or rollups actually are getting that. I thought in practice the batch poster was getting closer to 2x on non-specialized rollups <icemelon> > <icemelon> true. but the 4844 storage space is more scarse than calldata size (less than half of the size), which may drive the price of data blob to higher and close to calldata price (re @dankrad: actually 3 on average. Yes rollups will compete for 4844 blobs, just as they compete for calldata now) <sauliusgr> 32Kb/s is much more than caldata gives now <icemelon> > <icemelon> theoretically a block can hold up to 1.8MB of calldata, though avergage at about 90KB. But 4844 can only hold up to 0.75 MB per block and target at 0.375MB (re @sauliusgr: 32Kb/s is much more than caldata gives now) <sauliusgr> Yea, theoretically… <sauliusgr> The average block size is ~100kb? <icemelon> > <icemelon> actually the block size should be above 100kb now. checked a few recent blocks and all above 100 kb, and some is almost 700 kb (re @sauliusgr: The average block size is ~100kb?) <sauliusgr> I don’t expect that blob space will be dirty cheap, but it should be less expensive than calldata. And the price of calldata should be less then it is now. So sounds like an improvement.
